title: Alabama Medicaid ex parte renewal share, Aug. 2026
question: CMS State Medicaid and CHIP Eligibility Processing Data, Alabama state row, August 2026 reporting period, original first-print submission: ex parte renewals as a share of completed Medicaid renewals.
resolutionSource: CMS, State Medicaid and CHIP Eligibility Processing Data (data.medicaid.gov)
resolutionRule: Resolve to Alabama's August 2026 reporting-period original first-publication state row in the CMS State Medicaid and CHIP Eligibility Processing Data on data.medicaid.gov. Compute ex parte renewal share as the published ex parte renewal count divided by the published completed-renewal denominator, multiplied by 100 and rounded to one decimal percent. Use the first official CMS print available through the dataset; ignore later updated submissions or revisions. The registered ledger resolution date is 2026-12-15; I did not find a future-dated CMS release-calendar placeholder in this fast run, so this remains tied to the canonical target while the reasoning notes the schedule evidence limitation.

reasoning.result: Fetched five inspected Alabama original first-print observations rather than a complete monthly panel: 2025-07 = 51.6 percent, 2025-09 = 54.1 percent, 2025-11 = 55.8 percent, 2026-01 = 58.3 percent, and 2026-02 = 56.0 percent.

reasoning.text: Base-rate/reference class: the most relevant outside view is Alabama's own post-unwinding original first-print observations from July 2025 through February 2026, centered around 55.2 percent across the five inspected points and with a latest inspected value of 56.0 percent. I use Alabama persistence rather than a national average because this resolves one state row.

Level, momentum, and mechanism: the level is mid-to-high 50s; momentum from July 2025 to January 2026 was positive but February slipped to 56.0; one-off monthly cohort composition can move both completed-renewal and ex parte counts; the policy mechanism is continued CMS pressure for ex parte renewals but no known Alabama-specific automation shock in the checked context.

Prior/update/interval: prior model is latest-value persistence with a damped local trend, using the observed official-source-derived inspected sample for 2025-07, 2025-09, 2025-11, 2026-01, and 2026-02. The update adds +1.0 pp for the 2025-to-early-2026 improvement signal and +0.1 pp for CMS compliance pressure, partly offset by the February dip, moving 56.0 to 57.1. The 80% interval uses realized first-print swings in this Alabama sample, then widens for cohort mix and missing-month uncertainty.

Counter-consideration: upside outside the interval would require a sustained automation or data-match improvement pushing Alabama above roughly 62 percent. Downside outside the interval would require a manual-heavy renewal cohort, data-source outage, or operational regression pushing the share below roughly 52 percent. A schedule counter-consideration is that CMS publishes this series monthly but I did not verify a CMS page explicitly naming 2026-12-15 for the August 2026 first print.

Observed changes in the inspected Alabama sample were +2.5, +1.7, +2.5, and -2.3 pp, with mean absolute change about 2.25 pp and max absolute change 2.5 pp. Point calculation: latest 56.0 plus damped trend and operational-compliance adjustment of +1.1 pp equals 57.1 percent. Interval calculation: widen the observed 2.25 pp typical move by about 2.3 times for the longer August horizon, missing months, and renewal-cohort mix, giving lower half-width 5.2 pp and upper half-width 5.1 pp, or 51.9 to 62.2 after rounding.
